mainTopic: The errors of יואב and of שרו של רומי, and the laws of the עיר מקלט: burial, outskirts, the גואל הדם, and a tree on the boundary
overview: The amud opens by showing that both views on whether a disqualified כהן's כהונה is 'dead' or 'voided' can fit רבי יהושע. Then רב lists the mistakes יואב made when he grabbed the מזבח for safety, and אביי adds one more. ריש לקיש describes three mistakes the שרו של רומי will make when he seeks refuge in בצרה. Back in the משנה, רבי אבהו teaches that the ערי מקלט are not used for burial, except for the רוצח himself. The outskirts protect the רוצח, but he must live inside the city, and he may not even live in tunnels under the outskirts. The גמרא then discusses the רוצח who leaves the תחום. רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא argue whether killing him is a מצוה or only רשות for the גואל הדם, and רב follows רבי אליעזר that he may not be killed before a trial. Next the גמרא asks whether leaving the city by accident still exposes him, and whether a son can be the גואל הדם against his father. A new משנה rules that a tree on the boundary follows its branches. The גמרא compares this to מעשר שני, and רב כהנא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both views fit רבי יהושע, not a split between the two sages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier comparison. According to רבי אליעזר everyone agrees, and the dispute only exists according to רבי יהושע. The view that the כהונה is 'dead' fits him simply.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, everyone agrees. They only argue according to רבי יהושע. The one who says the כהונה is 'dead' follows רבי יהושע's plain view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that the 'dead' vs. 'voided' dispute is the same as the debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. It says the whole argument takes place inside רבי יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the 'voided' view was matched with רבי אליעזר and the 'dead' view with רבי יהושע. Now the גמרא says everyone agrees with the 'voided' outcome under רבי אליעזר. So the two sides only differ on how to understand רבי יהושע, and the 'dead' view simply follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (someone's opinion)
Everyone; all opinions
They disagree
'Dead': the כהונה ends from now on, but what was done before stays valid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two sides are just copying רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The גמרא is saying the opposite: both sides can agree with רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer
everyone does not disagree,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if you follow רבי אליעזר, both sides agree the כהונה is voided.

phrases.english: when they disagree, it is according to Rabbi Yehoshua:
the one who says 'dead' is in line with Rabbi Yehoshua,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison the גמרא made just before this piece.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the 'dead'/'voided' dispute matches the רבי אליעזר/רבי יהושע debate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי אליעזר there is no dispute at all, so the argument must sit within רבי יהושע's view.

steps.title: How the 'voided' view also fits רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The 'voided' view can say that רבי יהושע only validated a חלל's service because of the פסוק 'ברך ה׳ חילו'. About the status of the כהן himself, even רבי יהושע agrees the כהונה is voided.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'voided' will explain: רבי יהושע only said his view there, about the service, because the פסוק says 'Bless, ה׳, his strength, and accept the work of his hands.' This includes even the חללים among the כהנים. But here, even רבי יהושע agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the 'voided' view can also agree with רבי יהושע. It limits רבי יהושע's lenient ruling to the service itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's leniency comes from a special פסוק that accepts the service even of a חלל after the fact. That פסוק talks about the service, not the כהן's status. So about whether the כהן's כהונה was real, even רבי יהושע can agree it is voided backward.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Voided': the כהונה is cancelled backward, as if it never existed
He only said his view up to here: a way of limiting someone's ruling to its original case
'His strength/property'; read here as hinting to חללין
כהנים disqualified because of flawed lineage
Agrees; concedes

steps.whatToRemember: Both the 'dead' and 'voided' views can agree with רבי יהושע. His leniency covers only the service, which a פסוק protects, not the כהן's status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a sage's ruling is limited to the case where his special source applies.

phrases.english: And the one who says 'voided' —

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said so there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the service a disqualified כהן performed.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'Bless, Lord, his strength,
phrases.notes: דברים 33:11

phrases.english: and accept the work of his hands' —
even the disqualified ones among him,
phrases.notes: The word חֵילוֹ is read as if it hints to חֲלָלִין.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: but here, even Rabbi Yehoshua agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection by showing how the second view also fits רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a ruling to its source (עד כאן לא קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's leniency seemed to mean the כהונה was never voided backward.
steps.terutzMaskana: His leniency is limited to the service, because of the פסוק. On the כהן's status he agrees it is voided.

steps.title: רב: יואב made two mistakes when he fled to the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, רב says יואב made two mistakes when he fled and grabbed the horns of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If his verdict was decided…' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: יואב made two mistakes at that moment, as it says: 'And יואב fled to the Tent of ה׳ and grabbed the horns of the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה, which mentions יואב. It brings רב's claim that יואב made two mistakes. This sets up the next step, which lists the mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses יואב as an example of an important person who still cannot leave the עיר מקלט. רב uses the פסוק about יואב running to the מזבח to show he misunderstood how the מזבח protects a person.

keyTerms.meaning: His verdict was decided; the opening words of the line of the משנה being discussed
Mistakes; errors
The horns (raised corners) of the מזבח

phrases.english: 'His verdict was decided,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening words of the next part of the משנה, the part that mentions יואב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי טָעִיּוֹת טָעָה יוֹאָב בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה,
phrases.english: Joab made two mistakes at that moment,
as it is written: 'And Joab fled to the Tent of the Lord'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:28

phrases.english: 'and grabbed the horns of the altar,'

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי טָעִיּוֹת טָעָה יוֹאָב בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יואב made two mistakes when he grabbed the מזבח for protection.

steps.title: The two mistakes: the corners instead of the top, and שילה instead of the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: Only the top of the מזבח gives refuge, but יואב grabbed its corners. Only the מזבח of the בית המקדש gives refuge, but he grabbed the מזבח of שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He erred, because only its top gives refuge, and he grabbed its corners. He erred, because only the מזבח of the permanent Temple gives refuge, and he grabbed the מזבח of שילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the two mistakes רב mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each mistake follows a pattern: the rule is that only X protects, but יואב grabbed Y. The first mistake is about which part of the מזבח protects. The second is about which מזבח protects.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives refuge; protects
Its top (roof) of the מזבח
The permanent House, meaning the בית המקדש in ירושלים
The place where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He erred: for only its top gives refuge,
and he grabbed its horns.
He erred: for it only gives refuge
if it is the altar of the eternal House,
and he grabbed the altar of Shiloh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists the two mistakes announced in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the top of the מזבח of the בית המקדש gives refuge.

steps.title: אביי: יואב also erred because he was not a כהן
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the מזבח only protects a כהן who is in the middle of doing the service, and יואב was not a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: In this too he erred. It only gives refuge to a כהן with the service in his hand, and יואב was a זר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds one more mistake to רב's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's mistakes were about the place: which part of the מזבח and which מזבח. אביי adds a mistake about the person. Even the right spot protects only a כהן who is actively serving, and יואב was not a כהן at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a mistake
The service is in his hand; he is in the middle of the Temple service
A non-כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The מזבח's protection is very narrow: only its top, only in the בית המקדש, and (per אביי) only for a כהן who is serving. יואב failed on every count.

phrases.english: Abaye says:
In this too he erred:
He erred: for it only gives refuge
to a priest with the service in his hand,
and he was a non-priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אוֹמֵר: בְּהָא נָמֵי מִיטְעָא טְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another mistake to רב's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח only protects a כהן who is in the middle of the service.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the שרו של רומי will make three mistakes
steps.stepSummary: On the theme of mistakes about refuge, ריש לקיש says the angel of רומי will make three mistakes in the future, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו about בצרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The angel of רומי will make three mistakes in the future, as it says: 'Who is this coming from אדום, with stained clothes from בצרה?'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was discussing mistakes about refuge, it brings a related teaching from ריש לקיש. This step sets it up, and the next step lists the three mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes ה׳ coming from בצרה in אדום after taking revenge. ריש לקיש reads it to mean the angel of רומי (connected to אדום) will run to בצרה hoping for safety and fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The heavenly angel in charge of רומי
In the future; destined
אדום, linked with רומי
בצרה, a city of אדום

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
three mistakes is destined
the angel of Rome to make,
as it is written: 'Who is this who comes from Edom,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 63:1

phrases.english: 'with stained garments from Bozrah?'

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ טָעִיּוֹת עָתִיד שָׂרוֹ שֶׁל רוֹמִי לִטְעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related teaching about mistakes in seeking refuge, after יואב's mistakes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel of רומי will seek refuge in בצרה and make three mistakes.

steps.title: The three mistakes: wrong city, wrong kind of killer, wrong kind of being
steps.stepSummary: Refuge is in בצר, not בצרה. Refuge is only for a שוגג, but he killed on purpose. Refuge is only for a human, but he is an angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will err, because only בצר gives refuge, and he runs to בצרה. He will err, because it only protects one who killed by accident, and he killed on purpose. He will err, because it only protects a person, and he is an angel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists ריש לקיש's three mistakes, using the same 'only X protects, but he is Y' pattern as יואב's mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three mistakes cover the place, the act, and the person. בצר is a real עיר מקלט, but בצרה only sounds like it. Even in the right city, an עיר מקלט protects only a person who killed by accident, and an angel is not a person at all.

keyTerms.meaning: בצר, one of the ערי מקלט
Someone who killed by accident
Someone who killed on purpose
An angel

steps.whatToRemember: The rules of the עיר מקלט and the מזבח are exact. Being in a place that seems close or similar does not give protection, as both יואב and the שרו של רומי show.
steps.confusionAlert: בֶּצֶר (the real עיר מקלט) and בׇּצְרָה (the city in אדום) are different places. The mistake is exactly that they sound alike.

phrases.english: He errs: for only Bezer gives refuge,
and he goes into exile to Bozrah.
He errs: for it only gives refuge to an accidental killer,
and he was an intentional one.
He errs: for it only gives refuge to a person,
and he is an angel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists the three mistakes announced in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עיר מקלט protects only in בצר (not בצרה), only an accidental killer, and only a human.

steps.title: Cities of refuge are for living, not for burial
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns from a פסוק that the עָרֵי מִקְלָט were given for life, not as a place to bury people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: The cities of refuge were not given for burial. The פסוק says their open land is "for their cattle, their property, and all their animals (חַיָּתָם)." The word חַיָּתָם hints at חַיִּים, life. So the cities were given for living, not for burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and brings a new rule from רבי אבהו: people are not buried inside the עָרֵי מִקְלָט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עָרֵי מִקְלָט are cities of the לויים. The פסוק lists what the land around these cities is for, and the word חַיָּתָם is read as לְחַיִּים, "for life." Since burial is not on the list, the cities are not meant to be used for graves.

keyTerms.meaning: Cities of refuge, where someone who killed by accident can run to be safe
Burial
The open land around a city of the לויים
For life; here it is read into the word חַיָּתָם

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
Cities of refuge were not given for burial,
as it is written: "And their open land shall be for their cattle,
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:3

phrases.english: and for their property, and for all their animals" –
phrases.notes: The word חַיָּתָם sounds like חַיִּים, life. That is the hook for the next line.

phrases.english: for life they were given, and not for burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about mistaken refuge (Steps 6-7) and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עָרֵי מִקְלָט are not used for burial, because they were given 'for life.'

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה says the killer is buried there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו using the משנה's reading of "שָׁמָּה": the רוצח lives, dies, and is buried in the city of refuge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects: the פסוק says "there" (שָׁמָּה), and the משנה reads it as: there he will live, there he will die, there he will be buried!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אבהו's rule with a teaching that says burial does happen in the city of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו said there is no burial in these cities. But the word שָׁמָּה teaches that the רוצח is buried right there. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: "There"; the word in the פסוק about the city the רוצח fled to
Living place, home
Death

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "There" –
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25, the city the killer ran to.

phrases.english: there shall be his dwelling,
there shall be his death,
there shall be his burial!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's rule from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's rule that there is no burial in the עָרֵי מִקְלָט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word שָׁמָּה teaches that the רוצח is buried in the city, so some burial must happen there.

steps.title: The killer is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The רוצח is different, because the Torah spelled out that he is buried there. Everyone else follows רבי אבהו's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A killer is different, because the Torah told us about him specifically.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבהו by saying the רוצח is an exception the Torah wrote out on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule still holds: the עָרֵי מִקְלָט are not for burial. The רוצח alone is buried there, because the פסוק (שָׁמָּה) says so about him directly. The rule stays, and the רוצח is an exception to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different
The Torah ("the Merciful One") spelled it out about him
Here, someone who killed by accident

steps.whatToRemember: No one is buried in the עָרֵי מִקְלָט, except the רוצח himself, because the Torah said so about him.

phrases.english: A killer is different,
since the Merciful One revealed it about him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the challenge to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שָׁמָּה seemed to show that burial in these cities is allowed in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the רוצח is buried there, because the Torah singled him out. The general rule stands.

steps.title: Contradiction: does the outskirts protect or not?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the outskirts of the city protect the רוצח like the city does, but a ברייתא reads "in it" to mean only in the city and not in its outskirts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: just as the city protects him, so does its outskirts. But a teaching contradicts this: "and he shall live in it" means in it, and not in its outskirts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and sets it against a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the outskirts (תְּחוּם) like the city itself. The ברייתא reads the word בָּהּ (in it) as leaving out the outskirts. Both cannot be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes in and protects
And they pointed out a contradiction
The outskirts of the city, the area around it
"And he shall dwell in it"

phrases.english: Just as the city takes him in, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say that its outskirts take him in too.

phrases.english: And they pointed out a contradiction: "And he shall dwell in it" –
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.english: in it, and not in its outskirts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: another line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the outskirts protect like the city
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns from בָּהּ that the outskirts are left out, which clashes with the משנה.

steps.title: Protection versus living there
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the outskirts do protect the רוצח, but he may live only inside the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no contradiction. Here (the משנה) is about being protected. There (the ברייתא) is about where he may live.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction by showing that the two sources are talking about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the outskirts the גואל הדם may not kill him, so the outskirts protect. But the place he must actually live is inside the city itself. The word בָּהּ only limits where he lives.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
To take in and protect
To live, to make one's home

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult,
here – for protection,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה.

phrases.english: there – for living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into two different matters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the משנה and the ברייתא argue about whether the outskirts count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outskirts protect him, but he must live inside the city.

steps.title: Why do we need a rule about living there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need a פסוק to stop him from living in the outskirts. We already know you may not turn the open land into city or the city into open land.
steps.simpleTranslation: "For living"? Learn it from the rule that you may not turn a field into open land or open land into a field, and not open land into city or city into open land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions אביי's answer: the rule he gave seems to be already known from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land around a city of the לויים has a fixed purpose, and you may not change one kind of land into another. So no one could build a home in the open land anyway. Why would בָּהּ be needed to teach that the רוצח may not live there?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him learn it from (another source that already teaches it)
Field; the farmland further out from the city
One may not make, one may not change

phrases.english: "For living"?
Let him derive it from the fact
that one may not make a field into open land
nor open land into a field,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִגְרָשׁ עִיר וְלֹא עִיר מִגְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: nor open land into city, nor city into open land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for אביי's rule from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for בָּהּ to teach that he may not live in the outskirts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Building homes in the open land is already forbidden, so the פסוק seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The rule is needed for tunnels
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the rule is needed for living in tunnels under the open land, which do not change how the land looks or is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is needed only for tunnels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains what the פסוק adds: a case the land rule does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tunnel dug under the open land does not turn the open land into city, so the land rule would not forbid it. Without בָּהּ, the רוצח could have lived in such a tunnel. בָּהּ teaches that he must live inside the city itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for
Tunnels, underground spaces

steps.whatToRemember: The outskirts protect the רוצח, but he must live inside the city. The פסוק בָּהּ even stops him from living in a tunnel under the outskirts.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is needed only for tunnels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִמְחִילּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a case that only this source covers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The land rule seemed to make בָּהּ unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: בָּהּ is needed to stop him living in tunnels, which the land rule does not cover.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: a מצוה for the גואל הדם
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a רוצח who left the תחום, a ברייתא brings רבי יוסי הגלילי's view: the גואל הדם has a מצוה to kill him, and anyone else is allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a killer who went outside the boundary, etc. The רבנן taught: "And the blood redeemer kills the killer": it is a מצוה for the blood redeemer. If there is no blood redeemer, anyone is allowed to. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and brings a ברייתא with the first side of an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the רוצח leaves the outskirts, he is no longer protected. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the פסוק as a real מצוה for the גואל הדם. If there is none, any person is permitted, though not commanded.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood redeemer, the close relative of the person who was killed
A commandment, something one is required to do
Permission; allowed but not required

phrases.english: A killer who went outside the boundary, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
"And the blood redeemer kills the killer" –
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:27

phrases.english: it is a מצוה for the blood redeemer,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹאֵל הַדָּם – רְשׁוּת בְּיַד כׇּל אָדָם,
phrases.english: if there is no blood redeemer – it is permitted for any person,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁיָּצָא חוּץ לַתְּחוּם וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the תחום, killing the רוצח is a מצוה for the גואל הדם and permitted for anyone else.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: only permission, and others are liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees: the גואל הדם is only allowed to kill him, and anyone else who kills him is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: It is permitted for the blood redeemer, and every other person is liable for killing him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side of the argument, רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא is stricter. For the גואל הדם it is only רְשׁוּת (allowed), not a מצוה. Anyone else who kills the רוצח is guilty for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Are liable (guilty) for killing him

steps.whatToRemember: Outside the תחום: רבי יוסי הגלילי says a מצוה for the גואל הדם and permitted for others. רבי עקיבא says only permitted for the גואל הדם, and others are liable.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it is a מצוה for the גואל הדם and רְשׁוּת for anyone else. רבי עקיבא gives the גואל הדם only רְשׁוּת, and everyone else is guilty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
it is permitted for the blood redeemer,
and every other person is liable for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוסי הגלילי in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Killing the רוצח outside the תחום is only permitted for the גואל הדם, and others who kill him are liable.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that the גואל הדם has a מצוה to kill the רוצח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי הגלילי gets his idea that killing the רוצח outside the תחום is a real מצוה. This question sets up the next two steps, where each side explains its reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, רבי יוסי הגלילי said the גואל הדם has a מצוה. A מצוה needs a source in the פסוק, so the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the ברייתא brought in Steps 15–16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which wording in the פסוק makes killing the רוצח a מצוה?

steps.title: The verse says he kills, not if he kills
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads ורצח גאל הדם as a command, because the פסוק does not say 'if he kills'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'if he kills'? (No, it says 'and the גואל הדם kills', so it is a command.)
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי points out that the פסוק does not say 'if the גואל הדם kills him'. It says flatly 'and the גואל הדם kills', so he reads it as an instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק wanted to teach that killing is only allowed, it could have used 'if' language. The direct wording ורצח shows that the Torah wants it to happen, so it is a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (meaning: it is not written that way)
And the blood-redeemer kills (במדבר 35:27)

phrases.english: Is it written: "If he kills"?
phrases.notes: The פסוק (במדבר 35:27) says "ורצח גאל הדם", meaning "and the גואל הדם kills", with no "if" in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק uses direct wording instead of 'if' wording, so killing the רוצח is a מצוה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the verse does not say he shall kill
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the פסוק also does not say 'he shall kill' as a command, so it only gives permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא says: Is it written 'he shall kill'? (No, so it is only permission.)
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his own reading of the same words. The פסוק does not say 'he shall kill' as an order, so it is only describing something the גואל הדם is allowed to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages read the same word ורצח. רבי יוסי הגלילי notices that it is missing 'if', while רבי עקיבא notices that it is missing a clear command form. So רבי עקיבא concludes that killing is a רשות, only permission.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall kill (command form)
Permission (allowed, but not required)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת depends on how to read one word, ורצח. Is it a command, or only a description of what is allowed?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva says: Is it written: "He shall kill"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's opposite reading of the same פסוק discussed in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק has no command form, so killing the רוצח is only permitted.

steps.title: רב: the blood-redeemer is executed
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a גואל הדם kills a רוצח who went outside the תחום, the גואל הדם is executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא בר טוביה says in the name of רב: If a רוצח went outside the תחום, and the גואל הדם found him and killed him, the גואל הדם is executed for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב. A גואל הדם who kills the רוצח outside the תחום is treated as a murderer and gets the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is much stricter than both opinions in the ברייתא. Neither of them made the גואל הדם liable at all for killing a רוצח outside the תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the boundary (of the city of refuge)
He is executed for killing him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra bar Toviyya says that Rav says:
A killer who went out beyond the boundary,
and the blood-redeemer found him and killed him –
he is executed for him.
phrases.notes: "He" is the גואל הדם. He is put to death for killing the רוצח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling on the same case as the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גואל הדם who kills a רוצח outside the תחום is executed.

steps.title: רב's ruling matches neither opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: his ruling fits neither רבי יוסי הגלילי nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is not like רבי יוסי הגלילי and not like רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא רב is following. Both sages in the ברייתא allow the גואל הדם to kill, so רב seems to have no source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי calls it a מצוה and רבי עקיבא calls it a רשות. Neither one would ever give the גואל הדם the death penalty. An אמורא like רב needs a תנא to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

phrases.aramaic: לָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, וְלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא!
phrases.english: Not like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, and not like Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, וְלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the גואל הדם is executed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known תנאים allow the killing, so רב's ruling seems to go against every opinion.

steps.title: רב follows רבי אליעזר: no killing before trial
steps.stepSummary: רב follows רבי אליעזר, who learns from עד עמדו לפני העדה למשפט that the גואל הדם may not kill the רוצח before he has been judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב follows this תנא, as taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, why does the פסוק say 'until he stands before the congregation for judgment'? Since it says 'and the גואל הדם kills the רוצח', you might think he may do it right away. So the פסוק says 'until he stands before the congregation for judgment'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב follows a third תנא, רבי אליעזר. According to him, the גואל הדם may not kill the רוצח until a בית דין has judged him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that the permission of ורצח גאל הדם only starts after the trial. So a גואל הדם who kills a רוצח who has not yet been judged is a murderer and is executed. That is רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he stands before the congregation for judgment (במדבר 35:12)
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
One might have thought
Congregation (here, the בית דין)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר here is a different תנא from רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. רב is not choosing between those two. He follows a separate, third opinion.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the גואל הדם's permission depends on a trial happening first. Without a בית דין ruling, killing the רוצח is plain murder.

phrases.english: He said it in accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"Until he stands before the congregation for judgment,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:12

phrases.english: why does the verse need to say this?
Since it says:
"And the blood-redeemer kills the killer,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:27

phrases.english: one might think, right away?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עַד עׇמְדוֹ לִפְנֵי הָעֵדָה לַמִּשְׁפָּט״.
phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "Until he stands before the congregation for judgment."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by finding a תנא for רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different תנא who supports the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב goes against every known תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי אליעזר: the גואל הדם may not kill before a trial, so if he does, he is executed.

steps.title: What do the other sages learn from this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא learn from עד עמדו לפני העדה למשפט, since they do not use it the way רבי אליעזר does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי and רבי עקיבא, what do they learn from this 'until he stands before the congregation for judgment'?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the other two sages do not learn רבי אליעזר's rule from this פסוק, the גמרא asks what they use it for. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that no פסוק is extra. If a sage does not use a פסוק for one teaching, he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Akiva,
this "until he stands before the congregation for judgment"
what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הַאי עַד עׇמְדוֹ לִפְנֵי הָעֵדָה לַמִּשְׁפָּט מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the two sages of the ברייתא and asks how they use the פסוק from Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson do רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא take from עד עמדו לפני העדה למשפט?

steps.title: A court that witnessed the killing cannot judge it
steps.stepSummary: They use the פסוק for רבי עקיבא's teaching: if a סנהדרין saw someone kill, he must be judged by a different בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what is taught: רבי עקיבא says, how do we know that if a סנהדרין saw someone kill a person, they may not put him to death until he stands before another בית דין? Because the פסוק says 'until he stands before the congregation for judgment', meaning until he stands before another בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other sages use this פסוק for a different rule. Judges who saw the killing themselves cannot be the ones to judge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until he stands before the congregation' teach that there must be a proper trial before a בית דין that is judging him. Judges who were eyewitnesses cannot fill that role, so the case goes to another court.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
The court of judges that handles capital cases
A different court

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, עד עמדו לפני העדה למשפט, has two uses. For רבי אליעזר it means no killing before a trial. For רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא it means witnessing judges must hand the case to another court.

phrases.english: That is needed for that which is taught,
Rabbi Akiva says:
From where do we know about a Sanhedrin that saw
someone who killed a person
that they do not put him to death
until he stands in a different court?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עַד עׇמְדוֹ לִפְנֵי הָעֵדָה לַמִּשְׁפָּט״ –
phrases.english: The verse says: "Until he stands before the congregation for judgment" –
until he stands in a different court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that a סנהדרין which saw the killing must send the case to a different בית דין.

steps.title: Even leaving the city by accident lets the avenger kill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the doubled verb יָצֹא יֵצֵא that the גואל הדם may kill the רוצח even if he left the עיר מקלט unwittingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "If the murderer goes out." This would only teach that he left on purpose. How do we know the same is true if he left by accident? The פסוק says "if going out he goes out": in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the doubled wording of a פסוק to widen the law. The killer may be killed even if he left the city by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra word, we would only know the rule for a רוצח who left the city on purpose. The doubled verb יָצֹא יֵצֵא is read as adding the case of leaving by accident (בְּשׁוֹגֵג). So the ברייתא says it does not matter how he left.

keyTerms.meaning: "Going out, he goes out": a doubled verb in the פסוק
On purpose, deliberately
By accident, without meaning to
In any case, no matter how

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"If the murderer goes out"
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:26

phrases.english: I would only know if he left intentionally;
if he left unwittingly, from where do we know?
The verse states: "If going out he goes out"
phrases.notes: The verb is said twice, and the ברייתא learns something from the extra word.

phrases.english: in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִם יָצֹא יֵצֵא הָרֹצֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of a רוצח outside his city, now asking whether the way he left matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גואל הדם may kill the רוצח whether he left the עיר מקלט intentionally or unwittingly.

steps.title: A different ברייתא says killing him is punished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges with another ברייתא: someone who kills a רוצח who left by accident is executed if he did it on purpose, and exiled if he did it by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: the one who kills him on purpose is executed, and the one who kills him by accident is exiled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another ברייתא seems to say the opposite. Killing a רוצח who left by accident is treated like ordinary murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רוצח who left by accident were fair game, his killer would not be punished at all. This ברייתא punishes the killer fully: death for killing on purpose, גלות for killing by accident. So the two ברייתות contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Is executed
Goes into exile to an עיר מקלט

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
And one who kills him intentionally is executed,
phrases.notes: This is about a רוצח who left the city by accident, so killing him counts like killing anyone else.

phrases.english: and one who kills him unintentionally is exiled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a contradicting ברייתא against the ברייתא of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 25, which permits killing a רוצח who left unwittingly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא fully punishes whoever kills a רוצח who left unwittingly, so he cannot be fair game.

steps.title: The two ברייתות argue about reading doubled words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two ברייתות disagree over whether דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם, meaning whether the doubled verb teaches anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one follows the view that the Torah spoke in human language. That one follows the view that we do not say the Torah spoke in human language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות follow two different opinions about how to read the Torah's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion says a doubled verb is just normal speech and teaches nothing extra. On that view, only leaving on purpose lets the גואל הדם kill, which matches the second ברייתא. The other opinion reads every extra word as a teaching, so the doubled verb adds leaving by accident, which matches the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
The Torah spoke the way people speak, so repeated words are just style and teach nothing new
Following the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: The first הָא here means the second ברייתא, the one that punishes the killer. The second הָא means the first ברייתא, the one that learned from the doubled verb. The order is reversed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this follows the one who says:
phrases.notes: "This" is the second ברייתא, the one that punishes whoever kills him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִינַן דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: we say the Torah spoke in the language of people,
and that follows the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: we do not say the Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion (two different views on reading doubled words)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give contradictory rules for one case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow two opinions about whether a doubled verb teaches anything, so each one is consistent with its own view.

steps.title: אביי: the punishment for leaving should not be harsher than the original
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the view דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם makes more sense here, so that the רוצח's later punishment matches his original one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow the view that the Torah spoke in human language, so his end is not harsher than his beginning. At the beginning, if he killed on purpose he is executed, and if by accident he is exiled. So too at the end: if he leaves on purpose he is killed, and if he leaves by accident he is exiled.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a reason to prefer one side. A רוצח who leaves the city by accident should not lose his protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the רוצח first killed, the law separated on purpose (death) from by accident (גלות). אביי says the same split should apply when he leaves the city: leaving on purpose exposes him to the גואל הדם, but leaving by accident only sends him back into גלות. Otherwise an accident would end up punished more harshly than the original killing.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes more sense
So that his later punishment is not harsher than his first one

steps.whatToRemember: Following אביי, a רוצח who leaves the עיר מקלט by accident is still protected. Only leaving on purpose lets the גואל הדם kill him.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי turns a reading debate into a fairness rule: the law for leaving the city mirrors the law for the original killing.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It stands to reason

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: to follow the one who says the Torah spoke in the language of people,
so that his end will not be more severe than his beginning:
phrases.notes: "Beginning" is his punishment for the killing itself; "end" is what happens when he leaves the city.

phrases.english: just as at his beginning, intentionally he is executed,
unintentionally he is exiled,
so too at his end, intentionally he is killed,
unintentionally he is exiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Chooses between the two opinions presented in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The view דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם is more reasonable here: leaving on purpose lets the גואל הדם kill him, while leaving by accident only means גלות.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree: can a son be the avenger against his father?
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says that when a father kills, his son becomes his גואל הדם. Another ברייתא says the son does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a father who killed, his son becomes his גואל הדם. Another ברייתא teaches: his son does not become his גואל הדם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא sets two contradicting ברייתות side by side to prepare for the next step, where it suggests a way to explain them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a father who killed, for example his own son, so a surviving son is the victim's relative. One ברייתא lets that son act as גואל הדם against his own father. The other ברייתא does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood avenger: the victim's relative who may pursue the killer
The other one

phrases.english: It is taught in one ברייתא:
A father who killed,
phrases.notes: For example, he killed one of his sons, so a surviving son is a relative of the victim.

phrases.english: his son becomes his blood avenger.
And it is taught in another ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בְּנוֹ נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ גּוֹאֵל הַדָּם.
phrases.english: His son does not become his blood avenger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about who can serve as גואל הדם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two ברייתות disagree about whether a son can be the גואל הדם against his father.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about whether a son becomes גואל הדם against his father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא says the son becomes his father's גואל הדם and the other says he does not, so they seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: Linking the two ברייתות to רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא allowing the son follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, and the one forbidding him follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this one follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and that one follows רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the two ברייתות reflect the earlier argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. The לֵימָא form shows this is a suggestion that may still be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the sugya, רבי יוסי הגלילי held that killing the רוצח is a מִצְוָה for the גואל הדם, so even a son would be obligated. רבי עקיבא held it is only רְשׁוּת, merely permitted, so a son should not be the one to kill his father. The גמרא tries to explain the contradiction through this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion the גמרא may later reject
A commandment, an obligation
Permission only, not an obligation

phrases.english: Shall we say this follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא that lets the son be the avenger; רבי יוסי הגלילי called the killing a מצוה.

phrases.english: and that follows Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי וְהָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a way to explain the contradiction from step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two ברייתות about a son as גואל הדם reflect the argument between רבי יוסי הגלילי (מצוה) and רבי עקיבא (רשות).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different opinion (proposed, then rejected in step 31)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות about a son as גואל הדם contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: the ברייתא allowing the son follows רבי יוסי הגלילי (מצוה), and the one forbidding him follows רבי עקיבא (רשות). Step 31 rejects this.

steps.title: A son may never act against his father, so the suggestion fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea from step 30. Whether killing the רוצח is a מצוה or only a רשות, a son is never allowed to strike his father, except when the father is a מסית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really understand it that way? Whether killing the רוצח is a מצוה or only optional, is a son allowed to do it? But רבה בר רב הונא said, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: in every case, a son may not act as an agent to strike or curse his father, except for a מסית, because the Torah says 'You shall not spare nor conceal him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the suggestion that the two ברייתות follow רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. It shows that no opinion would let a son kill his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 tried to say that the ברייתא allowing the son follows the view that the גואל הדם has a מצוה to kill. But a son may not even give his father lashes or curse him for בית דין, so he surely may not kill him. The only exception is a מסית, because there the Torah says not to show him mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: "And can you really think so?" A phrase used to reject a suggestion
An obligation. Here: the גואל הדם is commanded to kill the רוצח
Optional. Here: the גואל הדם is allowed, but not required, to kill the רוצח
An agent. Here: someone who carries out בית דין's punishment
A person who tries to persuade others to worship idols

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this step says the son is never involved because of the מצוה/רשות dispute. The point is the opposite: that dispute does not matter, because a son's duty to honor his father blocks him either way.

phrases.english: And can you really understand it that way?
Both according to the one who says it is a מצוה
phrases.notes: This is the dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא from steps 15–16: must the גואל הדם kill the רוצח, or is he only allowed to?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רְשׁוּת, מִי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: and according to the one who says it is optional, is it permitted?
But didn't Rabba bar Rav Huna say,
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught the same:

phrases.aramaic: לַכֹּל אֵין הַבֵּן נַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלִיחַ לְאָבִיו
phrases.english: In all cases, a son does not become an agent against his father
phrases.notes: He means acting for בית דין, for example giving his father lashes as a punishment.

phrases.english: to strike him or to curse him,
except for one who incites to idol worship,
for the Torah said
"You shall not spare him nor cover up for him"!
phrases.notes: דברים 13:9

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ? בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִצְוָה בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רְשׁוּת, מִי שְׁרֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution suggested in step 30
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that the two ברייתות split along the רבי יוסי הגלילי / רבי עקיבא dispute
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under any view, a son may not strike his father (except a מסית), so no view could let a son act as גואל הדם against his father

steps.title: One teaching is about a son, the other about a grandson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction differently. The ברייתא that says no is about a son. The ברייתא that says yes is about a grandson.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difficulty: this ברייתא is about his son, and that ברייתא is about his son's son.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the earlier answer, the גמרא gives a new way to explain the two ברייתות from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות now agree. A son can never be גואל הדם against his own father. But a grandson can be גואל הדם against his grandfather. Now the ברייתות are talking about two different people, so they no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Brings a new answer after the earlier one was rejected
It is not difficult. The two sources do not really contradict
His son's son, meaning a grandson

steps.whatToRemember: A son may not be the גואל הדם against his father. A grandson may be the גואל הדם against his grandfather.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is about his son,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 29 that says the son does not become גואל הדם.

phrases.english: and that one is about his son's son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בִּבְנוֹ, וְהָא בְּבֶן בְּנוֹ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 31 rejected the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות argue over whether killing the רוצח is a מצוה or only a רשות
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree. A son may not be גואל הדם against his father, but a grandson may be against his grandfather

steps.title: A tree on the edge of the boundary follows its branches
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that if a tree is partly inside and partly outside the תחום of an עיר מקלט, the whole tree is judged by where its branches are.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A tree standing inside the boundary with its branches leaning outside, or standing outside with its branches leaning inside: everything follows the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a tree on the border of the protected area around an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the trunk is inside and the branches outside, or the other way around, the משנה gives one rule: the branches decide. If the branches are inside the תחום, the tree counts as inside and protects the רוצח. If they are outside, it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree
The boundary of the protected area around the עיר מקלט
The branches or top of a tree
Everything follows the branches

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides whether a רוצח standing in or under such a tree is protected from the גואל הדם.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A tree that stands within the boundary,
and its branches lean outside the boundary,
or it stands outside the boundary
and its branches lean within the boundary –
everything follows the branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אִילָן שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree on the border of the תחום of an עיר מקלט is judged entirely by its branches

steps.title: A different teaching splits the tree at the wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with another משנה about a tree on the wall of ירושלים. There, each part of the tree is judged by its own position compared to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They raised a contradiction: A tree standing inside and leaning outward, or standing outside and leaning inward: from the wall inward counts as inside, and from the wall outward counts as outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה (from מסכת מעשר שני, about the wall of ירושלים) that seems to clash with our משנה. This sets up a question the גמרא will need to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the whole tree follows its branches. The other משנה splits the tree at the line of the wall. Each part takes the status of the side it is on. So which rule is right for a tree on a border?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction. Introduces a source that seems to clash
A wall. Here: the wall of ירושלים
From the line of the wall
The second tithe, which must be eaten inside ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: The second משנה is not about an עיר מקלט at all. It is about where the wall of ירושלים ends for מעשר שני. The גמרא compares them because both ask how to treat a tree that crosses a border.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The source quoted next is a משנה about מעשר שני and the wall of ירושלים.

phrases.aramaic: אִילָן שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ הַפָּנִים וְנוֹטֶה לַחוּץ,
phrases.english: A tree that stands inside and leans outward,
or stands outside and leans inward,
from the line of the wall inward counts as inside,
from the line of the wall outward counts as outside!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי: אִילָן שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בְּתוֹךְ הַפָּנִים וְנוֹטֶה לַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from step 33
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that everything follows the branches (הכל הולך אחר הנוף)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה about a tree on a border splits the tree at the wall instead of letting the branches decide, which contradicts our משנה

steps.title: Tithe and refuge cities follow different rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 34. מעשר שני depends on the wall, so each part of the tree is judged by its own position. An עיר מקלט depends on living there, and a person can live in the branches but not in the trunk, so the branches decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you comparing מעשר to ערי מקלט? The תורה tied מעשר to the wall, but it tied ערי מקלט to living there. A person can live in the branches, but not in the trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question from step 34. It says you cannot compare the tree on the wall of ירושלים to the tree at an עיר מקלט, because the two laws are built on different ideas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעשר שני, the key is being inside the wall, so every part of the tree is judged by where it physically stands. For an עיר מקלט, the key is being able to live there and be protected. A person can sit and stay among the branches, but you cannot live inside a trunk, so the branches decide.

keyTerms.meaning: You are raising a contradiction (setting two sources against each other)
Here, מעשר שני: produce that must be eaten inside ירושלים
Cities of refuge, where an accidental killer is protected
Wall (of ירושלים)
Dwelling, living somewhere
The branches (canopy) / the trunk (the base of the tree)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key גמרא tool. Two cases that look alike can be ruled differently once you ask what each law actually depends on.

phrases.english: Are you raising a contradiction between tithe and cities of refuge?
For tithe, the Merciful One made it depend on the wall,
for cities of refuge, the Merciful One made it depend on dwelling —
in its branches one can live,
phrases.notes: Literally 'it can be lived in.' A person could actually stay up among the branches.

phrases.english: in its trunk one cannot live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: each law depends on a different criterion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tree on the wall of ירושלים and the tree at an עיר מקלט should follow the same rule
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר depends on the wall, so each part follows its own position. An עיר מקלט depends on living there, so the branches decide.

steps.title: A contradiction between two sources on tithe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now contrasts the משנה about the tree on the wall of ירושלים, where each part follows its own position, with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says that for ירושלים too, you follow the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now contrast tithe with tithe. A ברייתא teaches: in ירושלים, follow the branches; in ערי מקלט, follow the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. Even within the laws of מעשר, the sources seem to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 said that for מעשר each part of the tree is judged by its own position, based on the משנה from step 34. This ברייתא instead says that for ירושלים you follow the branches, just like for an עיר מקלט. So the two sources about מעשר contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Follow the branches: the canopy decides the status of the whole tree
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction between tithe and tithe,
phrases.notes: The first 'tithe' is the משנה from step 34, where each part of the tree goes by its own spot.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא: In Jerusalem — follow the branches,
in cities of refuge — follow the branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 35, a new contradiction appears within the laws of מעשר itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה about the tree on the wall of ירושלים (step 34)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה judges each part of the tree by its own position. The ברייתא says to follow the branches for ירושלים. Both rule on the same law of מעשר.

steps.title: Two sources, two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the two sources follow different opinions: one is רבי יהודה and the other is the רבנן. He begins quoting a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It is not difficult. This source is רבי יהודה, and that one is the רבנן, as a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources reflect a מחלוקת between תנאים. He is setting up the next move, a ברייתא that shows this מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing the two sources to agree, רב כהנא says they come from opposing views. Which source matches רבי יהודה and which matches the רבנן is not stated yet. The ברייתא that follows will make it clear.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the standard opening of an answer
This one ... and that one ...: assigning each source to a different case or opinion

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: It is not difficult,
this one is Rabbi Yehuda and that one is the Rabbis,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (a מחלוקת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא about מעשר contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not need to agree: one follows רבי יהודה and the other follows the רבנן
